Script.name: coords
Script.script:
--[[ Coordinates Sean Stoves, 2026-08-01
Aardwolf puts a coordinate on every room in the big open zones and tells you it on arrival:
Below the Basement Staircase {coords}0,30,20
'zone,x,y', or a bare '{coords}-1' where there is no grid. Seven zones turn up in a month of logs - 0 is the Aylor street grid and by a long way the most common, 4 the continent, 1/2/3/5 the oceans, 6 the air you fly through. This was called Vidblain for a while, which named the one place that never showed up in the sample.
The tag is always gagged. We took it off the tag gag's list so we could read it, so hiding it is our job now and has to happen whether or not we have anything to display.
The reading goes in a small draggable panel of its own, with the position as the title: there is nothing else to put in a box that size.
Vidblain is still why you'd want a target: it drops you somewhere random and every way out is a fixed coordinate - Omen Tor at 11,8, Fury City at 11,26. Those are preset; anywhere else, give it an x,y.
The axes, measured rather than assumed - 24,18 then 'run 2s5e' lands on 29,20, so x grows EAST and y grows SOUTH. y running southward is the surprising half and the reason this wasn't left to a guess.
The learning is still here and still runs: if any of that is ever wrong, one clean move corrects it and the correction sticks. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.coords = aardkit.coords or {}
local CO = aardkit.coords local U = aardkit.util.named("Coords")
local CFG = U.load("coords", { show = "coordareas", -- coordareas | always | off (when to fill the panel) marks = {}, -- name -> {x=,y=} target = nil, -- which compass direction each axis grows in; measured, and re-learned if a -- move ever disagrees axis = { xdir = "east", ydir = "south" }, })
CO.zone, CO.x, CO.y = nil, nil, nil
-- Consoleless: the title carries the reading, so there's nothing to put in a -- body. Small enough to tuck anywhere, and the panel manager remembers where. local panel = aardkit.panel.new({ name = "coords", title = "Location: -", x = "10px", y = "620px", width = 210, height = 34, consoleless = true, })
CO.panel = panel
local function settitle(txt) local h = panel and panel.holder if h and h.setTitle then pcall(function() h:setTitle(txt, "#3ad07a", "cb12") end) end end
local last = { x = nil, y = nil, dir = nil }
-- Aardwolf's own names for the places worth reaching, straight off 'speedwalks' local KNOWN = { ["omen tor"] = { 11, 8 }, ["asherodan"] = { 10, 15 }, ["darklight"] = { 14, 23 }, ["imperial"] = { 23, 4 }, ["sendhia"] = { 5, 6 }, ["fury"] = { 11, 26 }, }
local function inzone() return CO.zone ~= nil and CO.x ~= nil end
local function invidblain() local z = gmcp and gmcp.room and gmcp.room.info and gmcp.room.info.zone return z == "vidblain" end
--- -- axis learning -- -- One clean move teaches it: if east changed x by +1 then +x is east. Diagonals -- and anything that moved both axes are ignored - they'd teach it nothing. ---
local function learn(dx, dy, dir) local a = CFG.axis or {} local newdir if (dir == "east" or dir == "west") and dx ~= 0 and dy == 0 then newdir = (dx > 0) == (dir == "east") and "east" or "west" if a.xdir == newdir then return end -- already learned - don't hit disk on every step a.xdir = newdir elseif (dir == "north" or dir == "south") and dy ~= 0 and dx == 0 then newdir = (dy > 0) == (dir == "north") and "north" or "south" if a.ydir == newdir then return end a.ydir = newdir else return end CFG.axis = a U.save("coords", CFG) end
-- Ambiguity is sticky until a tag clears it. Toggling last.dir on truthiness -- only covered exactly two in-flight moves: a third arriving before any tag -- came back found it nil again, re-armed, and taught the axis from a direction -- that didn't produce that tag. Three in flight isn't exotic - the speedwalker -- sends a step every 0.25s regardless of whether the last one's tag has -- returned, so any lag over that stacks them up. -- -- on_coords clears both when a tag lands, so this only has to refuse to guess. function CO.on_move(dir) if last.dir ~= nil or last.muddled then last.dir, last.muddled = nil, true else last.dir = dir end end
--- -- the tag ---
function CO.on_coords(zone, x, y) -- Gag first and unconditionally. This used to sit inside the display path, -- so anywhere the panel had nothing to say the raw tag printed instead. U.gag() zone, x, y = tonumber(zone), tonumber(x), tonumber(y)
if last.x and x and last.dir then learn(x - last.x, y - last.y, last.dir) end last.x, last.y, last.dir, last.muddled = x, y, nil, false
CO.zone, CO.x, CO.y = zone, x, y CO.stamp() end
function CO.on_nocoords() U.gag() CO.zone, CO.x, CO.y = nil, nil, nil last.x, last.y = nil, nil settitle("Location: -") end
-- how far, and which way, to the active target function CO.delta() local t = CFG.target if not (t and inzone()) then return nil end local dx, dy = t.x - CO.x, t.y - CO.y if dx == 0 and dy == 0 then return "here" end
local a = CFG.axis if not (a and a.xdir and a.ydir) then return string.format("%+d,%+d", dx, dy) -- honest until it has learned end local out = {} if dx ~= 0 then local way = (dx > 0) and a.xdir or (a.xdir == "east" and "west" or "east") out[#out + 1] = math.abs(dx) .. way:sub(1, 1) end if dy ~= 0 then local way = (dy > 0) and a.ydir or (a.ydir == "north" and "south" or "north") out[#out + 1] = math.abs(dy) .. way:sub(1, 1) end return table.concat(out, " ") end
-- the delta as something you can actually type function CO.runcmd() local t = CFG.target local a = CFG.axis if not (t and a and a.xdir and a.ydir and inzone()) then return nil end local dx, dy = t.x - CO.x, t.y - CO.y if dx == 0 and dy == 0 then return nil end
local parts = {} if dy ~= 0 then local way = (dy > 0) and a.ydir or (a.ydir == "south" and "north" or "south") parts[#parts + 1] = math.abs(dy) .. way:sub(1, 1) end if dx ~= 0 then local way = (dx > 0) and a.xdir or (a.xdir == "east" and "west" or "east") parts[#parts + 1] = math.abs(dx) .. way:sub(1, 1) end return "run " .. table.concat(parts) end
--- -- the panel ---
function CO.stamp() -- 'off' used to save and then do nothing at all: the panel kept updating and -- the only way to be rid of it was 'panel coords hide'. -- panel:hide() saves panel state to disk unconditionally, so once it's -- already hidden don't call it again on every single room move. if CFG.show == "off" then if panel:visible() then panel:hide() end; return end
if not inzone() then settitle("Location: -"); return end if CFG.show == "coordareas" and not invidblain() then settitle(string.format("Location: %d,%d", CO.x, CO.y)) return end
local d = CO.delta() if d and d ~= "here" then settitle(string.format("%d,%d → %s", CO.x, CO.y, d)) elseif d == "here" then settitle(string.format("%d,%d arrived", CO.x, CO.y)) else settitle(string.format("Location: %d,%d", CO.x, CO.y)) end end
--- -- commands ---
function CO.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) -- 'x opacity 200' where somebody looks for it, rather than only -- 'panel x opacity 200'. One line; core does the work. if aardkit.panel.verb("coords", verb, rest) then return end
rest = U.trim(rest)
if verb == "" or verb == "status" then local rows = { { "here", inzone() and (CO.x .. "," .. CO.y .. " (zone " .. CO.zone .. ")") or "no coordinates here" }, { "target", CFG.target and (CFG.target.name .. " " .. CFG.target.x .. "," .. CFG.target.y) or "none" }, { "to go", CO.delta() or "-" }, { "axes", CFG.axis and ("+x " .. (CFG.axis.xdir or "?") .. ", +y " .. (CFG.axis.ydir or "?")) or "not learned yet - move once" }, { "run", CO.runcmd() or "-" }, { "show", CFG.show }, { "" }, } rows[#rows + 1] = { "Vidblain exits" } for k, v in pairs(KNOWN) do rows[#rows + 1] = { " " .. k, v[1] .. "," .. v[2] } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "coord <name|x,y>", "set the target and show the way" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "coord run", "send the run command for the straight line" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "coord clear", "drop the target" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "coord show off|coordareas|always", "when the panel has anything to say" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "coord panel [show|hide|dock|embed]", "move it or put it away" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "coord opacity <0-255>", "how solid this window is; 'default' follows the shared setting" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "", "'vid' still works if that's what your fingers type" } U.help("Coordinates", rows)
elseif verb == "run" or verb == "go" then local c = CO.runcmd() if not c then U.warn("No target, or you're already on it. 'coord omen tor' first.") else -- Vidblain is a maze, so this walks the straight line and the MUD -- gives up after three blocked moves. Run it again from wherever -- you end up; it's a nudge, not a pathfinder. U.ok(c) send(c, false) end
elseif verb == "clear" then CFG.target = nil; U.save("coords", CFG); U.ok("Target cleared.")
-- 'coord panel <verb>' rather than 'coord dock' etc, because 'coord show' is -- already the display mode and the two were colliding - the panel one was -- reachable only as the undiscoverable 'vid show2'. elseif verb == "panel" then if rest == "" then rest = "toggle" end aardkit.panel.cmd("coords " .. rest)
elseif verb == "show" then if rest == "off" or rest == "always" or rest == "coordareas" then CFG.show = rest; U.save("coords", CFG) if rest ~= "off" then panel:show() end CO.stamp() U.ok("Coordinates: " .. rest .. ".") else U.warn("coord show off|coordareas|always") end
else local x, y = arg:match("^%s*(%-?%d+)%s*,%s*(%-?%d+)%s*$") local found if x then found = { name = x .. "," .. y, x = tonumber(x), y = tonumber(y) } else local k = arg:lower() if KNOWN[k] then found = { name = k, x = KNOWN[k][1], y = KNOWN[k][2] } else -- substring fallback, but only when it's unambiguous - pairs() -- iteration order over KNOWN isn't guaranteed, so a bare substring -- match used to resolve to whichever name the hash visited first, -- and something like 'r' matches 5 of the 6 names local hits = {} for name in pairs(KNOWN) do if name:find(k, 1, true) then hits[#hits + 1] = name end end if #hits > 1 then table.sort(hits) U.warn("'" .. arg .. "' matches " .. table.concat(hits, ", ") .. " - be more specific.") return elseif #hits == 1 then found = { name = hits[1], x = KNOWN[hits[1]][1], y = KNOWN[hits[1]][2] } end end end if not found then U.warn("Don't know '" .. arg .. "'. Try 'coord' for the list, or 'coord 11,8'.") return end CFG.target = found U.save("coords", CFG) U.ok("Target " .. CFG.target.name .. " at " .. CFG.target.x .. "," .. CFG.target.y .. (CO.delta() and (" - " .. CO.delta()) or "")) end end
-- Mudlet doesn't say which way you went, but it does say what you sent, and -- that's enough: one plain 'east' with a clean coordinate change teaches it. local DIRS = { n = "north", north = "north", s = "south", south = "south", e = "east", east = "east", w = "west", west = "west", }
U.killhandler(aardkit_coords_send) aardkit_coords_send = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysDataSendRequest", "aardkit.coords.on_send")
function CO.on_send(_, cmd) local d = DIRS[U.trim(tostring(cmd or "")):lower()] if d then CO.on_move(d) end end
aardkit.register("coord", "where you are on the Aardwolf grid, and how far to a target", CO.cmd)
